paragraphs: HaNoiTVEdu is a workplace learning platform designed to help Hanoi TV employees build practical AI skills for their everyday work.
We focus on role-based, hands-on learning for Editorial, Admin and Content teams — helping employees understand when to use AI, which tools fit different tasks, and how to use them responsibly.
Through short learning modules, practical exercises, AI tool guidance and peer sharing, HaNoiTVEdu turns AI from a new technology into a practical work skill.

notebook.heading: PROMPT - LEARNING
notebook.lead: Your go-to collection of ready-to-use prompts for common Admin, Editor and Content tasks.

cards.title: EDITORIAL

ai-research-planning.title: RESEARCH PLANNING
ai-research-planning.subtitle: Turn a broad topic into a clear research plan

overview.label: OVERVIEW
overview.text: Research becomes time-consuming when you start searching without knowing exactly what you need to find. AI can help you plan your research first by turning one broad topic into focused questions, useful search keywords and information gaps.

what_you_will_learn.label: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN
items: Research Questions - Break a broad topic into clear questions you need to answer.
Search Keywords - Turn those questions into specific terms for more focused searching.
Information Gaps - Identify what you still need to find or verify.
Research Structure - Organise your research before spending time searching.

lead.title: First, tell AI what you're trying to do.
lead.text: Don't just give AI a topic. Give it topic + purpose, so it understands what kind of research you need. A breaking-news brief, an investigative feature, or an in-depth analysis will need very different questions even for the same topic.

bad.label: ✕ INSTEAD OF:
bad.text: “Tell me about Hanoi's new electric bus.”

good.label: ✓ TRY:
good.text: “I need to research Hanoi's new electric bus route for a news article.”

blocks.caption: A SECOND EXAMPLE: SAME TOPIC, DIFFERENT PURPOSE, DIFFERENT RESULT:
columns: TYPE OF QUESTIONS AI WILL PRIORITIZE

cells: Who, what, when: core facts needed immediately
Why, who benefits, long-term impact, comparison with similar cases
Open-ended questions to draw out perspective, contradictions to clarify with the source

tip.label: TIP FOR EDITORIAL TEAMS
tip.text: If the piece has a tight deadline, say so in the prompt (“300-word brief, due in 1 hour”).

lead.title: Turn one broad topic into specific questions.

blocks.label: Ask AI:
blocks.text: “Generate 5 key questions I should investigate about Hanoi’s new electric bus route.”

rows.text: Who is responsible for operating and funding it?
What are the operating hours and frequency?
Why is the route being introduced now?

blocks.text: Instead of searching randomly, you now have a clear list of what you need to find out.

tip.label: TIP FOR EDITORIAL TEAMS
tip.text: For time-sensitive news, ask AI to rank the questions by priority (which need answering before publishing, which can be added later). This keeps you from burning your time budget on secondary details.

lead.title: Turn questions into searchable terms.
lead.text: Your research question tells you what you need to know. Search keywords help you find that information.

blocks.label: Ask AI:
blocks.text: “Generate 3-5 specific search keywords for each research question."

You can adjust keywords based on the sources and information you find along the way.
This is a loop, not a one-time step.

tip.label: TIP FOR EDITORIAL TEAMS
tip.text: Try keywords in both Vietnamese and English if the topic has an international angle (e.g., foreign sponsors, imported technology), and favor keywords with proper nouns, numbers, and specific dates. They filter out much more accurate results than generic terms.

lead.title: Before finalizing your plan, ask: "What am I missing?"

blocks.label: Give your research questions to AI and ask:
blocks.text: "What important information might still be missing from this research plan?"

blocks.title: NEXT TO-DO LIST
blocks.text: These gaps become your next to-do list — what to search for or verify further.

tip.label: TIP FOR EDITORIAL TEAMS
tip.text: This step is often skipped under deadline pressure, but it is crucial for avoiding under-verified stories. Make it mandatory before a piece goes to edit.

key_idea.label: KEY IDEA
key_idea.text: Good research finds answers. Great research finds what's missing.

lessons.title: COMMON MISTAKES WHEN USING AI FOR PLANNING

rows.title: Accepting AI’s first set of questions without editing
rows.text: AI doesn’t know who your readers are, or what your newsroom has already published on the topic. Always review the question list and drop anything already answered or irrelevant to your angle.

rows.title: Stopping after one round of Q&A
rows.text: A solid research plan usually needs 2-3 rounds with AI: ask → review results → ask again to dig deeper or narrow scope. Don’t treat the first answer as the final plan.

rows.title: Using overly generic keywords
rows.text: “Hanoi electric bus” will surface thousands of results not specifically about the new route. The more specific (route name, timeframe, agency name), the more reliable the search results.

rows.title: Skipping the gap-check step due to time pressure
rows.text: This is the most common and riskiest mistake — it leads to publishing stories missing key information that a single question could have caught early.

rows.title: Confusing “AI asks good questions” with “AI gives correct answers”
rows.text: AI is good at suggesting what to ask, but not reliable when it answers those questions itself. Keep these two things clearly separated in your workflow.

tip.label: TIP FOR EDITORIAL TEAMS
tip.text: Avoid these mistakes to make AI a reliable partner in your editorial planning process, not a shortcut that leads to incomplete or risky stories.

key_idea.label: KEY IDEA
key_idea.text: Use AI to ask smarter questions, not to replace critical thinking.

lead.title: Use AI before you start searching

steps.label: QUESTION
steps.text: What do I need to find out?

steps.label: GAP CHECK
steps.text: What information am I still missing?

blocks.text: This gives you a clear research direction before you dive into browsing dozens of sources: saving time and reducing the risk of missing important details.

blocks.label: IMPORTANT:
blocks.title: AI IS YOUR ASSISTANT, NOT A REPLACEMENT
blocks.text: AI can help you plan and structure research, but it does not replace actual research.
blocks.chain: AI plans → You search → You verify
blocks.note: For editorial work, the human remains responsible for checking sources and deciding what can be used.
blocks.emphasis: AI should never be cited as a source itself. It’s a thinking tool to use before real research begins.

key_idea.label: KEY IDEA
key_idea.text: AI plans → You search → You verify

blocks.title: Before moving from "planning" to "actually searching," make sure:
items: You've stated the topic + purpose clearly (piece type, length, target audience)
You have at least 5 research questions, with duplicates or already-known answers removed
Each question has 2–3 specific search keywords attached
You've asked AI about information gaps and noted at least 3 items
You've clearly separated assumptions still needing verification from facts with an official source
Nothing in the plan is treated as "verified" simply because AI produced it

blocks.label: SKILL UNLOCKED:
blocks.title: AI RESEARCH PLANNING
blocks.banner: You can now use AI to:
blocks.text: You've learned how to turn a broad topic into a structured research plan before spending time searching.
If any item on this list isn't done yet, don't start writing - go back to the relevant step.

blocks.title: NEXT: 02 · SEARCH - AI-Assisted Search
blocks.text: Learn how to use AI to find relevant sources while keeping the original source and evidence at the center of your research.

lead.title: Take a few minutes now - the better your plan, the easier your research.

your_turn.label: YOUR TURN
your_turn.intro: Choose one topic from your current work. Ask AI to:

fallback.title: DON'T HAVE A TOPIC YET? TRY ONE OF THESE:
items: A new policy or regulation about to take effect
A local event or festival coming up in your area
A tech or consumer trend currently being discussed
A person or business about to be featured in the news

copy_prompt.text: "I need to research [TOPIC] for [PURPOSE]. Generate 5 key research questions, relevant search keywords for each question, and identify 3 important pieces of information I may still need to verify."

follow_up.label: FOLLOW-UP PROMPT
follow_up.hint: (use after you get the first results):
follow_up.text: "Of these 5 questions, which is most important if I only have 1 hour to research? Rank them by priority and briefly explain why."

quiz.title: QUICK CHECK
quiz.banner: Before you unlock the next skill...

questions.text: What should you do before searching for information?

options.text: Ask AI to write the whole article
Define what you need to find

questions.text: What is the purpose of research questions?

options.text: To identify what information you need to investigate

questions.text: Can AI-generated research questions be treated as verified information?

options.text: No - they are a starting point for research

footer.label: KEEP GOING!
footer.text: Good research starts with a plan. Answering these questions correctly means you're ready to unlock the next skill!
